segments.source: During the Whitsuntide festivities, about fifteen young girls, mostly Christian Gipsies, one of whom personates the Standard-bearer, another the King, and another the Queen ( kralyitza ), veiled and attended by a number of Maids of Honour, pass from door to door through the village, singing and dancing.
Their songs relate to such subjects as marriage, the choice of a husband or wife, the happiness of wedded life, the blessing of having children.
After each verse of their songs follows a refrain, Lado, oy, Lado-leh! which is probably the name of the ancient Slavonic Deity of Love.
